artifacts.summary: Research finding a tier-1 pull-side freshness detector already exists but fires only once per top-level command, not per skill dispatch; recommends moving the existing check (no new algorithm) into skill_preflight_update and surfacing it in the dispatch brief, with cost measured at ~130ms per invocation.

memory_candidates.content: The agent-system's consumer-deploy-freshness mechanism already has a per-extension, path-scoped pull-side check (check-deploy-freshness.sh + scripts/lib/deploy-freshness-lib.sh, backed by state.lua's mark_loaded stamping source_git_head into .claude-extensions.json on every load), wired into command-gate-in.sh's CHECKPOINT 1. It is NOT purely opt-in/report-only (that description fits only the fleet-wide check-consumer-freshness.sh behind --consumer-report). The real gap is granularity: command-gate-in.sh fires once per top-level command, not once per skill/agent dispatch, so a long /orchestrate run's later-spawned subagents never see a fresh check or its warning. skill_preflight_update in skill-base.sh runs once per skill dispatch and is the correct finer-grained hook point for this class of check.

The per-extension source_git_head freshness comparison (path-scoped git log -1 over an extension's whole source_dir) already catches single-file partial staleness within an extension directory -- any one file's change moves the recomputed head for the entire extension. A new whole-tree or per-file fingerprint/hash mechanism is redundant with this existing comparison; reuse deploy_freshness_status/deploy_freshness_stale_names from scripts/lib/deploy-freshness-lib.sh rather than inventing a second algorithm.

orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh already injects several context blocks into per-dispatch brief files (memory-context, literature briefing, hard-mode contract block, effort block) before an agent reads them. This is the precedented, low-cost injection point for surfacing any new per-dispatch signal (e.g. a deploy-freshness warning) directly into the context a spawned subagent reads, rather than only into the top-level orchestrating session's own stderr where a spawned subagent never sees it.
